subject.title: [Feature]: Auto‑forward images from Node agent.request to IM users when deliver: true

question: Should Node `agent.request` grow an explicit media-forwarding contract, or should callers use existing direct `send` and message-tool media delivery for dumb relay workflows?
rationale: The source path is clear, but choosing to forward node-originated attachments changes a security-sensitive gateway-to-IM delivery contract and cannot be resolved safely by automation.

options.title: Approve explicit opt-in relay
options.body: Add a narrowly scoped protocol field with authorization, media limits, audit behavior, target scoping, idempotency, and agent override or suppression semantics before implementation.

options.title: Keep agent-authored delivery only
options.body: Leave `agent.request` attachments as model input and tell relay callers to use the direct `send` RPC or message tool for media delivery.

options.title: Allow fallback forwarding
options.body: Automatically append original attachments when the agent returns no media, accepting the higher risk of surprising cross-boundary sends and delivery-contract drift.

recommendation.title: Approve explicit opt-in relay
recommendation.body: Add a narrowly scoped protocol field with authorization, media limits, audit behavior, target scoping, idempotency, and agent override or suppression semantics before implementation.

likelyOwner.reason: Peter has the broadest current blame and feature-history signal across the node-event, gateway media, protocol, and delivery files involved in this policy choice.
